# GymButt – full content

> GymButt is an iPhone app for strength training made in Switzerland. Users log sets, weights and reps; with every workout their avatar "Butt" earns XP, levels up and unlocks new items (caps, hairstyles, glasses, outfits, fur colors). Free without ads or account. Without the optional features Butties (friend groups) and Strava, workout data stays on the iPhone. Optional subscription GymButt Pro. Available on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/gymbutt/id6824511814 . Available in German and English. Not available on Android.

Key facts:
- Over 300 exercises with figures, instructions and common mistakes; ready-made workouts for beginner, intermediate and pro with bodyweight, free weights or machines
- Rest timer on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island, weight suggestions, plate calculator, supersets, cardio with time and distance
- Streaks with rest days and freezes; weekly and monthly challenges; levels and items are never lost
- Muscle map, personal records, import from Strong and Hevy (CSV), steps and cardio from Apple Health, send workouts to Strava
- Butties: private groups of up to 6 people, avatars side by side, no leaderboard, no public profiles (requires Sign in with Apple)
- Over 100 recipes (vegan, vegetarian, with meat) with a daily protein target
- GymButt Pro (Apple subscription, CHF 3 per month or CHF 25 per year in Switzerland, 7-day free trial): workout generation, weekly/monthly reports, strength check, nutrition profile with macros, all recipes, up to 3 Butties groups
- Developer: Moritz Härri, contact gymbutt@outlook.com

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/compare/

GymButt vs. Strong vs. Hevy
Three gym apps, three ideas. Which one fits you?
In short
Strong is a minimal workout log, Hevy a tracker with a social feed. GymButt is for people who need motivation: an avatar gets new items with every workout, friends train in small groups without a leaderboard, and your data stays on your iPhone without an account.
At a glance
GymButt Strong Hevy
Sets, weights, reps Yes Yes Yes
Platform iPhone iPhone, Android iPhone, Android
Avatar with items and levels Yes No No
Social Groups of up to 6, no leaderboard – Feed with followers
Recipes and protein target Yes No No
Use without an account Yes – –
Import from the other apps Strong and Hevy – –
Details about Strong and Hevy to the best of our knowledge, as of November 2026. "–" means not checked or not the app's focus.
When GymButt fits
When you know what you want to do at the gym but don't always go. GymButt rewards every workout with XP and new items for Butt, protects your streak with rest days and freezes, and the muscle map shows what fell short this week. If you train with friends, Butties shows who has already been, without comparing yourself to strangers.
When Strong fits
When you want a quick, no-frills log and don't need extras.
When Hevy fits
When you want to share your workouts publicly and follow others.
Switch without losing data
Export your workouts from Strong or Hevy as a CSV file and open it in GymButt under Settings › Import. GymButt calculates your records and weight suggestions from the imported history.
Questions about the comparison
What's the difference between GymButt, Strong and Hevy?
All three log strength training with sets, weights and reps. Strong is minimal and focused on logging, Hevy has a social feed with followers. GymButt focuses on motivation: an avatar gets new items with every workout, friends train in small groups without a leaderboard, and there are recipes with a protein target.
Can I switch from Strong or Hevy to GymButt?
Yes. GymButt imports the CSV export files from Strong and Hevy. Your workouts show up in the history and count toward records and weight suggestions.
Which gym app is best for beginners?
For beginners who struggle with motivation, GymButt is a good fit: ready-made beginner workouts, over 300 exercises with figures and instructions, and a streak with rest days that doesn't punish breaks. If you just want to jot down numbers quickly, Strong works well too.
Get Butt off the couch
GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/faq/

FAQ
Everything important about GymButt, answered briefly.
What is GymButt?
GymButt is an iPhone app for strength training. You log sets, weights and reps, and with every workout your avatar Butt earns XP, levels up and unlocks new outfits, hairstyles and items.
Is GymButt free?
Yes. Workouts, over 300 exercises, templates, the avatar, streaks and history are free and ad-free. The optional GymButt Pro subscription adds extra features.
What does GymButt Pro include?
Pro adds workout generation, weekly and monthly reports, the strength check, a nutrition profile with daily needs and macros, all recipes and up to three Butties groups. The subscription runs through Apple and comes with a 7-day free trial.
Do I need an account?
No. Without an account your workout data stays on your iPhone. You only need an account via Sign in with Apple for Butties, the groups with friends.
What happens to my data?
Workouts, weights, body weight, nutrition and Apple Health data stay on your iPhone. There are no ads, no tracking and no analytics tools. Without Butties and Strava, nothing leaves your iPhone. In Butties, only members of your groups see your nickname, your Butt, level, streak, whether you trained today and your number for the weekly challenge (e.g. 12 leg sets). Weights and health data don't go to Butties. If you send a workout to Strava, exercises, sets, reps and weights go to Strava. The privacy policy has all the details.
Is GymButt available on Android?
Not yet. GymButt currently runs on iPhone only.
Where can I get GymButt?
GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone. The core features are free, without ads and without an account. The optional GymButt Pro subscription adds more.
How does Butt get new items?
Every workout earns XP. New levels, achievements like a streak record or new personal bests, weekly challenges and the monthly challenge unlock caps, hairstyles, glasses, outfits and fur colors.
What happens if I take a break?
Rest days are planned in and don't hurt your streak, and there are freezes too. After several days without any movement Butt gets lazy and slumps on the couch. Levels and items are never lost, and one workout cheers Butt right up.
Is GymButt good for beginners?
Yes. There are ready-made beginner workouts with bodyweight, free weights or machines. Every exercise has a figure, short instructions and common mistakes.
Can I import my data from Strong or Hevy?
Yes. Import the CSV export from Strong or Hevy in the settings. Imported workouts show up in your history and count toward records and weight suggestions.
What are Butties?
Butties are small groups of up to six people. Your avatars stand side by side, you see who trained this week and can cheer each other on. There is deliberately no leaderboard and no public profiles.
Does GymButt work with Strava and Apple Health?
Yes. Steps and cardio workouts come from Apple Health. You can send a strength workout to Strava if you want, with duration and exercise list.
Can I log cardio?
Yes. Treadmill, rowing machine, cycling and more with time and distance, and the stair climber with floors.
Which languages is GymButt available in?
German and English.
Who makes GymButt?
GymButt is developed by Moritz Härri in Switzerland. Contact: gymbutt@outlook.com.
Another question? Write to gymbutt@outlook.com .
Get Butt off the couch
GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/beginner-workout-plan/

Guides › Training
Beginner workout plan
3 days a week, two alternating full-body plans, about 45 minutes per workout.
In short
As a beginner, train your whole body three times a week , for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Alternate between plan A and plan B, do 3 sets of 8 to 12 reps and add weight once you hit 12 in every set.
Why full body?
As a beginner you learn movements fastest by practicing them often. With a full-body plan every muscle group gets worked two to three times a week, and one missed session doesn't throw you off. The WHO recommends that adults train all major muscle groups on at least two days a week.
Plan A
Exercise Sets × reps Rest
Goblet squat 3 × 8–12 90 s
Bench press or push-ups 3 × 8–12 90 s
Seated cable row 3 × 8–12 90 s
Dumbbell shoulder press 2 × 10–12 60 s
Plank 3 × 20–40 s 45 s
Plan B
Exercise Sets × reps Rest
Dumbbell Romanian deadlift 3 × 8–12 90 s
Lat pulldown 3 × 8–12 90 s
Lunges 2 × 10 per leg 60 s
Incline dumbbell press 3 × 8–12 90 s
Dead bug 3 × 10 per side 45 s
What a week looks like
Week 1: Monday A, Wednesday B, Friday A. Week 2: Monday B, Wednesday A, Friday B. Rest days in between, where a walk or an easy bike ride is enough.
How heavy?
Pick a weight where the last two reps are hard but clean. Once you hit 12 reps in every set, add about 2.5 kg (5 lb) next time and start again at 8. That way you progress step by step without guessing.
Common beginner mistakes
Starting too heavy: technique first, the weight will follow.
Doing something different every time: stick with one plan for 8 to 12 weeks or you won't see progress.
Not logging: without notes you won't remember next week what you lifted.
Skipping rest days: muscles grow during recovery, not during the workout.
With GymButt
GymButt has ready-made beginner workouts with bodyweight, free weights or machines. It shows a figure with instructions for every exercise, remembers your last weight and suggests when to go heavier. Rest days count toward your streak, and Butt earns XP and new items for every workout.
FAQ
How often should beginners work out?
Two to three full-body workouts a week with at least one rest day in between is plenty at first. The WHO recommends muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days a week for adults.
How many sets and reps for beginners?
A good start is 2 to 3 sets per exercise with 8 to 12 reps and 1 to 2 minutes of rest. The weight is right when the last two reps are hard but clean.
When should I increase the weight?
Once you hit 12 clean reps in every set, add about 2.5 kg (5 lb) next time, or the next step on dumbbells, and start again at 8.
Source: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour (2020). This plan doesn't replace advice for pain or medical conditions.
Get Butt off the couch
GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/first-week-at-the-gym/

Guides › First week at the gym
First week at the gym
You don't need to know everything. You just need to start and show up three times.
In short
In your first week plan three training days with rest days in between, start with a ready-made beginner workout , log every set and deliberately use light weights. The goal of week one isn't performance, it's making the trip to the gym a habit.
The day before
Download GymButt, open Settings and choose your training days , for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Then pick a ready-made beginner workout. They come with bodyweight, free weights or machines, depending on what your gym has. Pack water and a towel and put the time in your calendar.
Monday: first workout
Do the workout exercise by exercise. Every exercise has a figure, instructions and common mistakes. Start light, 3 sets of 8 to 12 reps, and stop when you notice your form slipping. The rest timer runs on your Lock Screen, so you don't have to keep the app open. Afterwards your Butt earns its first XP.
Tuesday: rest day
You don't have to do anything. A rest day counts for your streak and even gives XP. Light movement like a walk doesn't hurt but isn't required. Sore muscles on day two are normal.
Wednesday and Friday
Repeat the workout. GymButt suggests a weight for next time. If you manage 12 clean reps in every set, you can add weight. If you want more variety, alternate between two workouts, as described in the beginner workout plan .
Weekend: look back
Check your history: how many workouts, how many sets? The muscle map shows which muscles you hit. A workout is done when you did it, even if it was short.
Common beginner mistakes
Starting too heavy and quitting after two weeks.
Training every day with no rest days.
Comparing yourself with others at the gym.
Not writing anything down, because without numbers you can't see progress.
With GymButt
When motivation dips, use the minimum goal: 20 minutes or three exercises. It counts for your streak, and you've done your workout. More in the motivation guide .
FAQ
How often should I go to the gym in my first week?
Three times is enough, for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Rest days in between let your muscles recover.
What weight should I start with?
A light weight you can lift cleanly 12 times. GymButt suggests weights afterwards. You can add weight once you manage 12 reps in every set.
Do I need to know everything in the first week?
No. You learn the exercises over time. In GymButt every exercise has a figure, instructions and common mistakes.
Get Butt off the couch
GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/gym-app-no-account/

Guides › Gym app with no account
A gym app with no account and no ads
You shouldn't have to sign up to train. Here is what GymButt sends where, and what it doesn't.
In short
Without the optional features Butties and Strava , workouts, weights, nutrition and steps stay on your iPhone . GymButt has no ads and no analytics . You only need an account for Butties, the groups with friends.
What stays on your iPhone
Workouts, weights, nutrition, history and records are stored locally on your iPhone. GymButt needs no account or email address for that. The app reads steps from Apple Health, but only if you allow it.
What GymButt doesn't have
No ads, in any version.
No analytics and no tracking of app usage.
No public profiles and no leaderboard.
What Butties stores
Only if you use Butties and sign in with Apple, GymButt stores your nickname, your Butt, level and streak, your daily status and your weekly challenge number at Google Firebase in Zurich. The members of your group can see these. If you send a Buddy a workout template, it stays on the server for 30 days at most, until it's accepted or declined. You delete your Butties account yourself in the app under “GymButties”.
What Strava gets
If you connect Strava, a workout only goes to Strava when you send it: name, start time, duration and exercises with sets, reps and weights. Your Strava sign-in is kept in your iPhone's Keychain.
How to check for yourself
The full explanation is in the privacy policy . In the App Store, the “App Privacy” section shows which data is collected. gymbutt@outlook.com answers questions.
With GymButt
You can use GymButt entirely without an account: train, keep your streak, dress up Butt and cook recipes. The groups with friends are there when you want them.
FAQ
Do I need an account for GymButt?
No. You only sign in with Apple for Butties, the groups with friends. Everything else works without an account.
Does GymButt have ads or tracking?
No. GymButt has no ads in any version and no analytics of app usage.
Where is my workout data stored?
On your iPhone. Without Butties and Strava, workouts, weights, nutrition and steps don't leave the device.
Get Butt off the couch
GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/gym-motivation/

Guides › Motivation
Sticking with the gym
Motivation is a bad training plan. These eight habits work even on tired days.
In short
People who stick with it don't rely on motivation but on fixed training days, a small minimum goal and planned rest days . A missed workout isn't a problem as long as the next one happens. Friends and visible progress make it easier.
1. Fixed days instead of "when I have time"
Pick two or three days and put them in your calendar like an appointment. "Monday, Wednesday, Friday after work" is easier to keep than "three times a week".
2. A minimum goal that always works
On bad days the rule is: 20 minutes or three exercises. Once you're changed and at the gym, you usually do more. And if not, you still hit your minimum.
3. Plan your rest days
A plan without breaks falls apart at the first cold. Planned rest days are part of training and don't feel like failure.
4. Never miss twice in a row
Missing a workout happens. In a study on habit formation (Lally et al., 2010), a single missed day didn't disrupt the habit. What matters is the next session.
5. Decide the workout in advance
If you only figure out at the gym what to do today, you lose time and energy. A fixed plan with exercises and weights makes the decision for you.
6. Make progress visible
Muscles grow slowly, numbers don't. Seeing your deadlift go from 40 to 60 kg brings you back next week.
7. Train with friends
People cancel plans with others less often than plans with themselves. It doesn't have to be the same gym: it's enough to see that the others have already trained today.
8. Small rewards
A check mark in the calendar, a streak or a new item for your avatar: small, immediate rewards make the start easier until training runs on its own.
With GymButt
GymButt is built around these ideas: a weekly plan with rest days, streaks with freezes, reminders only on training days, history with records and Butties groups with friends. For every workout, Butt earns XP and new items like caps, hairstyles and outfits.
FAQ
What should I do when I have no motivation for the gym?
Don't rely on motivation. Rely on fixed training days and a small minimum goal, for example just 20 minutes. Most of the time you end up training longer. Planned rest days, a training partner and visible progress help too.
How long does it take for exercise to become a habit?
In a study by Lally et al. (2010) it took 66 days on average for a new behavior to become automatic, with a wide range from 18 to 254 days. Missing a single day didn't break the habit.
Is it bad to miss a workout?
No. A single missed day hardly matters. What counts is training again at the next planned session. Just don't miss two workouts in a row.
Source: Lally P et al., European Journal of Social Psychology 2010, "How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world".

GymButt is free on the App Store, for iPhone.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/gymbutt-pro/

Guides › GymButt Pro
GymButt Pro
The essentials are free. Pro is for everyone who wants to look deeper into their training.
In short
In Switzerland GymButt Pro costs CHF 3 a month or CHF 25 a year , with a 7-day free trial . It adds reports, strength check, workout generation, a nutrition profile and more. Workouts, avatar, streak and history stay free, without ads.
What does Pro cost?
GymButt Pro is a subscription through Apple, monthly or yearly: CHF 3 a month or CHF 25 a year . The yearly plan is almost a third cheaper than twelve months (CHF 36). The first 7 days are free. Prices in other countries are shown by the App Store in your currency.
The subscription renews automatically unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before it ends in your Apple account settings.
What stays free?
The basics are free and ad-free: workouts, over 300 exercises, templates, rest timer, avatar with items, streak, challenges, history with records and muscle map, one Butties group, import from Strong and Hevy and five recipes per diet.
What does Pro add?
Generate a workout: pick muscle groups, duration and level, and the workout is ready.
Weekly and monthly report: comparison with previous weeks, sets per muscle and a focus for next week.
Strength check: a strength level per exercise, goals with a forecast and help on plateaus.
Volume trends, recap and CSV export.
Recovery per muscle on the muscle map.
Nutrition profile: your weight and goal become protein and calories per day and per meal.
All recipes instead of five per diet.
Two freezes per month instead of one and up to three Butties groups instead of one.
Who is it worth it for?
If you mainly want to log workouts and dress up your Butt, the free version is enough. Pro is worth it if you want to know whether you're getting stronger and where you stall, if you'd rather not plan your own workouts, or if you want your nutrition to follow your goal. Try the 7 days and decide afterwards.
How to cancel
On your iPhone open Settings, tap your name at the top, then “Subscriptions” and choose GymButt Pro. You can cancel there at any time. Pro stays active until the end of the paid period.
With GymButt
The Pro features open where you need them, for example in History under “View stats” for the strength check. You can see what's behind it before you subscribe.
FAQ
How much does GymButt Pro cost?
CHF 3 a month or CHF 25 a year in Switzerland, with a 7-day free trial. In other countries the App Store shows the price in the local currency.
Can I use GymButt without Pro?
Yes. Workouts, exercises, avatar, streak, history and Butties (one group) are free and ad-free.
How do I cancel GymButt Pro?
In your iPhone settings under your name › Subscriptions › GymButt Pro, at least 24 hours before it ends. Pro stays active until the end of the paid period.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/protein-per-day/

Guides › Nutrition
Protein per day
How much you really need to build muscle, and what that looks like on your plate.
In short
With strength training, about 1.6 g of protein per kg of body weight per day (0.7 g per lb) is enough. Up to 2.2 g per kg can make sense, especially while dieting. More brings hardly any extra muscle. Without training, the general recommendation for adults is 0.8 g per kg.
What the research says
A large analysis of 49 studies (Morton et al., 2018) found that extra protein improves muscle gains from strength training, but the effect levels off at around 1.6 g per kg per day. The International Society of Sports Nutrition recommends 1.4 to 2.0 g per kg for people who exercise. While dieting, the upper end helps preserve muscle.
How to work out your needs
Body weight 1.6 g/kg 2.0 g/kg
55 kg (121 lb) 88 g 110 g
65 kg (143 lb) 104 g 130 g
75 kg (165 lb) 120 g 150 g
85 kg (187 lb) 136 g 170 g
95 kg (209 lb) 152 g 190 g
Spread it over your meals
Three to four meals with 25 to 40 g of protein each are easier than one huge portion at night. Example for about 120 g:
Breakfast: 250 g low-fat quark or skyr with berries and oats (about 35 g)
Lunch: lentil bowl with tofu (about 35 g)
Snack: 2 eggs and a yogurt (about 20 g)
Dinner: salmon or chicken with rice and vegetables (about 35 g)
Vegan or vegetarian?
Works just as well. Combine legumes, tofu, tempeh, seitan and grains over the day and you get all the amino acids. Plant protein is slightly less well absorbed, so aim for the upper value.
With GymButt
GymButt calculates your daily protein target from your body weight and goal (2.0 g per kg to build muscle or lose weight, 1.6 g per kg to maintain) and has over 100 simple recipes, vegan, vegetarian or with meat, with a shopping list and cooking mode.
FAQ
How much protein do I need per day to build muscle?
If you do strength training, you need about 1.6 g of protein per kg of body weight per day (about 0.7 g per lb). Research shows little extra muscle gain above roughly 2.2 g per kg.
How much protein is that at 70 kg?
At 70 kg (154 lb), 1.6 g per kg is about 112 g of protein per day, spread over three to four meals with 25 to 40 g each.
Do I need protein powder?
No. Protein powder is convenient but not necessary. Quark or skyr, yogurt, eggs, legumes, tofu, fish and meat are enough if every meal has a protein source.
Sources: Morton RW et al., British Journal of Sports Medicine 2018, "A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength". Jäger R et al., Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition 2017, "Position stand: protein and exercise". If you have kidney disease, check with a doctor first.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/streak-with-rest-days/

Guides › Streak with rest days
Streak with rest days
A streak should get you to the gym, not give you a guilty conscience.
In short
In GymButt a day counts for your streak if you trained, hit your step goal or it's a planned rest day . If you miss a training day, a freeze covers it: one per month, two with Pro. You never lose levels or items.
The problem with the classic streak
Many apps only count days with a workout. If you take your rest days, you lose the chain. That rewards the wrong thing: you train sick or exhausted just to keep a number going. Rest days are part of training because muscles recover between sessions.
How the streak works in GymButt
In Settings you choose your training days , for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
All other days are rest days . They count for your streak and even give XP.
Reaching your step goal also keeps the streak going.
If you miss a training day, a freeze covers it. You get one per month, two with Pro.
If a training day is still open, GymButt reminds you at 8 pm.
What happens when the streak breaks?
You start again from zero, but you lose nothing: levels and items stay . Only Butt's mood drops when several days pass without movement. The streak is a rhythm, not a punishment.
Why this works
A study on habit formation (Lally et al., 2010) found that a single missed day didn't destroy the habit. What counts is being back at your next planned workout. A streak that plans for breaks reflects that.
Streak with friends
A Butties group has a shared streak. It grows every day on which everyone has trained or has a rest day. Once a week one person can miss with a freeze without breaking the chain. There is deliberately no leaderboard.
With GymButt
Plan training days you can manage even on bad days. Two or three are enough to start. The rest are rest days, and they count.
FAQ
Do rest days count for the streak?
Yes. Planned rest days count for your streak and even give XP. You choose which days are training days in Settings.
How many freezes do I get?
One freeze per month for free, two per month with GymButt Pro. It automatically covers a missed training day.
Do I lose levels or items when the streak breaks?
No. Breaks never cost levels or items. Only Butt's mood drops after several days without movement.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/guides/switch-from-strong-hevy/

Guides › Switch from Strong or Hevy
Switch from Strong or Hevy to GymButt
Your history stays: export it as a CSV and bring it into GymButt in three steps.
In short
Export your workouts from Strong or Hevy as a CSV file and pick it in GymButt under Settings › Bring over from Strong or Hevy . The workouts show up in your history and count for records and weight suggestions. XP is only for workouts you do in GymButt.
Step 1: export from Strong or Hevy
Both apps can export your workouts as a CSV file. You find the export in each app's settings: in Hevy under “Export & Import Data”, in Strong under “Export Strong Data”. Menu names can change with app updates. Save the file in Files or send it to yourself so you can pick it on your iPhone.
Step 2: import in GymButt
Open Settings in GymButt and tap Choose CSV file in the “Bring over from Strong or Hevy” section. GymButt recognizes which app the file comes from and first shows how many workouts and sets there are and which period they cover. Tap “Bring over” to start the import.
What happens
The workouts appear in your history and count for personal records and weight suggestions .
Imported workouts earn no XP . XP is only for workouts in GymButt.
If a workout is already in GymButt, it is skipped , so nothing gets imported twice.
If GymButt doesn't know an exercise, it adds it as your own exercise .
Weights in pounds are converted to kilograms.
If the file isn't from Strong or Hevy, you get an error message and your data stays unchanged.
And the way back?
With GymButt Pro you can share all your workouts with every set as a CSV file, for example for your coach or for Excel. According to the app, Strong and Hevy can import that file too. Your data stays yours.
With GymButt
After the import you can see at a glance how your training has gone so far, and GymButt suggests fitting weights for next time. Your Butt starts at zero because XP and items are only for workouts in GymButt. That makes the switch feel like a fresh start, not like falling behind.
FAQ
Will I lose my records if I switch?
No. Imported workouts count for records and weight suggestions in GymButt. Your data in Strong or Hevy also stays until you delete it there.
Does the import cost anything?
No. Importing from Strong and Hevy is free, without GymButt Pro.
Do I get XP for old workouts?
No. XP and items are only for workouts you do in GymButt. Imported workouts are marked “Imported from Strong · no XP” (or Hevy) in the history.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/

Off the couch, into the gym
GymButt is the gym app for iPhone where your avatar gets new outfits and items with every workout.

All features
No account · no ads · workouts stay on your iPhone
+100 XP
In short
GymButt is a workout tracker for strength training with over 300 exercises, a rest timer and weight suggestions. On top of that there's Butt: every workout earns XP, a new level and items like caps, hairstyles and fur colors. It keeps you going when motivation runs low.
Three reasons to keep going
Stress-free at the gym
Ready-made workouts for beginners to pros, over 300 exercises with instructions, a rest timer on your Lock Screen and the weight to use next time.
Streaks with rest days
Rest days and freezes protect your streak. Butt only gets lazy after several days without any movement, and one workout brings Butt right back.
Muscle map and records
See which muscles you trained this week, track records per exercise and import your history from Strong or Hevy.
Built for the bench
Big buttons, few taps per set
Your last weight is already filled in
Plate calculator and supersets
Cardio, steps from Apple Health
Share a workout as an image or send it to Strava
Butties
Start a group with up to five friends and invite them with a code. Your Butts stand side by side, you see who trained this week and cheer each other on. No leaderboard.
Monthly challenge Complete three tasks in a month to win that month's item.
FAQ
Is GymButt free?
Yes. Workouts, exercises, the avatar and streaks are free and ad-free. The optional GymButt Pro subscription adds weekly and monthly reports, the strength check, workout generation and all recipes.
Do I need an account?
No. Without an account your workout data stays on your iPhone. You only need an account for Butties, the groups with friends.
Is GymButt on Android?
Not yet. GymButt currently runs on iPhone only.

## https://gymbutt.ch/en/press/

Press
Official images, app icon and copy for GymButt. Feel free to use everything when writing about the app.
Short description
GymButt is an iPhone app for strength training from Switzerland. You log sets, weights and reps, and with every workout the avatar Butt earns XP, levels up and unlocks new items like caps, hairstyles and fur colors. Free, with no ads and no account.
Facts
Name GymButt
Platform iPhone (iOS)
Status Available on the App Store (iPhone), free, optional GymButt Pro subscription
Price Free, optional GymButt Pro subscription
Languages German, English
Exercises over 300
Developer Moritz Härri, Zurich
Contact gymbutt@outlook.com
Website gymbutt.ch
Longer description
Butt is your training buddy and a bit lazy at first. Every workout earns XP: Butt levels up and collects outfits, hairstyles, glasses and fur colors, looking funnier and funnier over time. Skip several days without any movement and you'll find Butt on the couch. Levels and items are never lost, though.
Underneath is a full workout tracker: ready-made workouts for beginners to pros, over 300 exercises with figures and instructions, a rest timer on the Lock Screen, weight suggestions, a muscle map, records and import from Strong and Hevy. In Butties, small groups of friends train together without a leaderboard. Workouts, weights and health data stay on the iPhone.
